newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to pick GM or Daewoo by March.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to pick GM or Daewoo by March.

text.p: Ukraine is trying to choose between U.S. carmaker General Motors and South Korea's Daewoo Group to invest in its AvtoZAZ car plant and the decision should be taken by March.

Valery Malev, the minister in charge of machine building, the military and conversion, said in an interview late on Thursday that a field of six investors including Renault and Peugeot of France, Italy's Fiat and South Korea's Hyundai had been narrowed down to two.

"There is no scheduled date for the final announcement. We are considering the proposals fully. But we expect to finalise the tender and announce the winner by the end of the first quarter of this year -- in March," Malev said.
Two years ago Ukraine began looking for an investor for the plant in the eastern industrial city of Zaporizhya two years ago. AvtoZAZ needs more than $1 billion in the next few years.
Daewoo was favoured to win until General Motors entered the race in June.
"Daewoo and General Motors are the most serious competitors and the strongest candidates," said Olexander Sotnikov, AvtoZAZ's General Director.

President Leonid Kuchma visited Daewoo's headquarters while on a visit to South Korea in December. He later met Daewoo's President Kim U Jung in Kiev and criticised the government for "giving preference to one of the competing companies".
GM has been lobbying heavily with the Ukrainian government.

AvtoZAZ began production in 1963 and has an annual capacity of 150,000 cars. But last year output fell to 6,881 compared to 1992's level of 130,000 cars, Oleh Kovalenko, head of the AvtoZAZ office in Kiev said on Friday.
"We are almost at a standstill. We have been seriously hurt by Ukraine's economic crisis," he added.
But he added that their new assembly line was built in 1994 and had Italian equipment which was still in perfect condition.
Eventually, said Malev, Ukraine would produce 250,000-300,000 cars a year. "Our car market's prospects are amazing. Investors will not be frustrated."
Government sources said GM foresaw production of 25,000 Opel Vectras a year, increasing to 40,000 cars. They said GM wanted to produce 70,000-80,000 Ukrainian Tavria small city cars.
Sotnikov said AvtoZAZ disagreed with GM's output forecasts and wanted to produce no less than 100,000 cars a year.
Daewoo's proposal is for 100,000 Tavrias a year and to start assembling three models of its own within 18 months, he said.
But Sotnikov said Daewoo's sales forecasts were low and its proposal for a return of investments in 12 years was too long.
Malev said AvtoZAZ would need some $1 billion in three to four years. "Our condition is that 70 percent of all spare parts and materials are to be made in Ukraine," he said.
"We need a fully-fledged domestic production."
Kiev officials from the two foreign carmakers were not prepared to comment while talks continued with the government.
But Kovalenko said Daewoo was seeking $300 per car produced.

The key difference in General Motors' approach was that Daewoo was aiming at customers in Ukraine and other members of the Commonwealth of Independent States while GM wanted to export Opels to Europe and elsewhere, he added.
